questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, in the context of the RBI's recent clarifications on forex hedging and reserve norms. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve is maintained by authorised dealer banks with the RBI under powers granted by the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
Authorised dealer banks are permitted to deal in foreign exchange only after obtaining a licence from the RBI under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Current account transactions under FEMA are, as a general rule, freely permitted unless specifically restricted by rules framed by the Central Government.
The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), 1973.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: RBI's FERR directions and AD bank licensing both flow from FEMA, current account transactions are presumptively free unless restricted, and FEMA 1999 replaced the stricter FERA 1973. Statement 2 is wrong because AD bank authorisation to deal in forex is granted under Section 10 of FEMA, not the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, which governs banking business generally, not foreign exchange dealing specifically.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: RBI's new forex reserve rules explained: FAQs on the 20% requirement, $2 million threshold and exemptions
questions.pyqLink: Tests FEMA 1999 vs FERA 1973 and AD bank licensing basics, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on capital/current account transaction classification under FEMA.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's direct tax system, in the context of the net direct tax collection data released for FY27. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is a direct tax levied on transactions in listed securities and is administered by the Income Tax Department.
Corporate tax is levied on the income of domestic and foreign companies operating in India under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Personal income tax in India is administered by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs.
Net direct tax collection is computed by adding refunds issued to the gross direct tax collected.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because personal income tax is administered by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), not the CBIC, which handles indirect taxes like GST and customs. Statement 4 is wrong because net direct tax collection is gross collection minus refunds issued, not plus, as also shown by the FY27 data where gross (₹16.03 lakh crore) minus refunds (₹2.65 lakh crore) gives the net figure (₹13.38 lakh crore).
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Net direct tax collections up 13.2% at ₹13.38 tn, corporate tax buoys
questions.pyqLink: Tests the direct-vs-indirect tax classification and CBDT/CBIC jurisdiction, a recurring static concept behind budget and revenue-collection news.

questions.stem: With reference to the Reserve Bank of India, which is issuing fresh regulatory norms on forex reserves and hedging, consider the following statements: 1. The Reserve Bank of India was established as a statutory body under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and is not a constitutional body. 2. The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is appointed by the President of India on the advice of the Union Cabinet. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Reserve Bank of India was established as a statutory body under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and is not a constitutional body.
The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is appointed by the President of India on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct; the RBI is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament, unlike bodies such as the Election Commission which are constitutional. Statement 2 is wrong because the RBI Governor is appointed by the Central Government (through the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet), not by the President of India.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: RBI issues clarifications on forex hedging curbs
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory vs constitutional body distinction and appointment procedure for the RBI Governor, a frequently tested institutional-detail area.

questions.stem: With reference to the Bretton Woods institutions, in the context of Finance Minister Sitharaman's address at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, consider the following statements: 1. The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank were both established following the Bretton Woods Conference of 1944. 2. The Development Committee is a joint ministerial forum of the IMF and the World Bank Group that advises on development issues. 3. India's voting share in the IMF is determined solely by its share of global merchandise trade. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank were both established following the Bretton Woods Conference of 1944.
The Development Committee is a joint ministerial forum of the IMF and the World Bank Group that advises on development issues.
India's voting share in the IMF is determined solely by its share of global merchandise trade.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, as confirmed by the Development Committee Plenary meeting referenced in the article. Statement 3 is wrong because IMF quota and voting shares are determined by a weighted quota formula combining GDP, economic openness, variability and reserves, not merchandise trade share alone.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Put private sector at center of development agenda: Sitharaman to World Bank
questions.pyqLink: Tests the structure and functions of Bretton Woods institutions, a recurring IR/Economy crossover static topic in UPSC Prelims.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of diseases and their mode of transmission/vector, in the context of India's disease surveillance data on malaria, dengue, kala-azar and rabies. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito, dengue by the Aedes mosquito, and kala-azar by the bite of an infected female sandfly (Phlebotomus) — all correctly matched. Rabies is transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected mammal, typically dogs, not through houseflies, making the fourth pair incorrect.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Mismatch in data on rabies deaths poses major challenge
questions.pyqLink: Tests vector-borne vs non-vector-borne disease transmission, a recurring static health/biology area triggered by disease surveillance news.

questions.stem: With reference to India's September trade data showing a widened trade gap, which one of the following best describes the term 'merchandise trade deficit'?
options: The excess of a country's total imports of goods and services over its total exports of goods and services during a period, also called the current account deficit
The excess of a country's imports of goods over its exports of goods during a period, forming part of the current account but excluding trade in services
The shortfall in foreign exchange reserves required to finance a country's import bill for three months
The gap between a country's total government revenue and expenditure financed through external borrowing
questions.explanation: Merchandise trade deficit specifically refers to the gap between a country's goods imports and goods exports, as reported separately from services trade by the commerce ministry; it is a sub-component of the current account, not the current account deficit itself. Option A wrongly conflates it with the broader current account deficit, option C describes import cover of forex reserves, and option D describes the fiscal deficit.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's merchandise trade deficit widens to $30.21 billion in September
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between merchandise trade deficit, overall trade deficit (goods+services) and current account deficit, a recurring BoP concept.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements in the context of the IMF's endorsement of India's revised GDP methodology. Statement-I: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation revised India's GDP calculation methodology, and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed this revision as consistent with international statistical best practices. Statement-II: A country's measured GDP growth rate for a given period is sensitive to the base year and compilation methodology used, since a change in either can alter the measured growth rate without any change in underlying real economic activity. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct, as the IMF's Asia-Pacific Director confirmed the revised GDP methodology was consistent with its advice. Statement-II is also a correct general statistical principle about GDP compilation. However, Statement-II explains why methodology changes are scrutinised in general, not specifically why the IMF chose to endorse India's particular revision, so it is not the correct explanation of Statement-I.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: IMF backs India's revised GDP methodology, projects it to overtake Japan as 4th-largest economy in 2027
questions.pyqLink: Tests understanding of GDP base-year revision and real vs measured growth, following the Statement-I/II format introduced from 2022 onward.

questions.stem: With reference to the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Election Commission of India became a multi-member body on a permanent basis from 1993 onwards, with each Election Commissioner having an equal vote in decision-making.

Under the Constitution, both the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners can be removed from office only through a resolution of Parliament in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the Commission became a permanent three-member body from October 1993, with decisions taken by majority when there is a difference of opinion, as per the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 324(5) protects only the CEC with a Supreme Court judge-like removal process; the other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC, which is the asymmetry opposition leaders cited while alleging that the CEC sidelined his colleagues during the SIR exercise.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Gyanesh Kumar undermined Election Commission’s independence: Sachin Pilot
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 324 and the CEC-vs-EC removal asymmetry, a recurring static fact (cf. UPSC 2017 question on Election Commission removal procedure)

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's steel sector and its decarbonisation targets:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: India's steel sector accounts for nearly 12% of the country's total greenhouse gas emissions.
India is currently the world's largest producer of crude steel.
The National Mission on Green Steel aims to lower the emissions intensity of crude steel production to 2.2 tonnes of CO2-equivalent per tonne by 2029-30.
India has committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: steel accounts for ~12% of India's GHG emissions, and the National Mission on Green Steel targets an emissions intensity of 2.2 tCO2e/tonne by 2029-30. Statement 2 is wrong since India is the second-largest crude steel producer, behind China. Statement 4 is wrong because India's net-zero target is 2070, not 2050.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India can cut steel emissions before new coal plants lock them in
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's climate commitments and industrial decarbonisation missions, an economy-environment fusion theme frequently seen since the Panchamrit pledges at COP26

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of species and their habitat/geographic association as reported in recent studies on habitat fragmentation:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Found mostly to the south of the Brahmaputra river in Northeast India
Habitat fragmented by coffee and tea estates around Valparai, Tamil Nadu
Native to the rainforests of Central America
Found in the rainforests of Central America
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched as per the article. Pair 3 is incorrect: the slow loris is native to Southeast Asia (including Indonesia), not Central America — the three-toed sloth, not the slow loris, is the Central American species facing fragmentation.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Building bridges for India's wildlife
questions.pyqLink: Tests species-habitat identification and habitat fragmentation as a conservation concept, similar to UPSC's recurring 'species in news' pairs format

questions.stem: With reference to artificial intelligence, which one of the following best describes an 'open-weight' model, such as the one recently released by Meta?
options: A model whose source code and training datasets are made fully public for anyone to inspect and modify
A model whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and run, even though the training code or underlying data may remain proprietary
A model that can only be accessed through a paid Application Programming Interface with no option for local deployment
A model developed entirely through crowdsourced computing power contributed by volunteer users worldwide
questions.explanation: An open-weight model releases its trained parameters (weights) for download and local use, even though the company may keep its training code, data, or full source closed — exactly what Meta did with Muse Spark Open. Option A describes a fully open-source model, which is a stricter and different category; option C describes a closed, API-only model, the opposite case; option D describes distributed/crowdsourced computing, unrelated to weight release.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Meta releases weights for Muse Spark Open
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static distinction between open-source and open-weight AI models, a concept UPSC has begun probing as AI governance enters the GS-III syllabus

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Jewish community associated with Kochi, Kerala:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Cochin Jews are considered one of the oldest Jewish communities in India, with a presence in Kerala going back many centuries.
The Paradesi Synagogue in Kochi, built in 1568, is regarded as the oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth of Nations.
Following the formation of Israel in 1948, a majority of Cochin Jews emigrated from Kerala to Israel.
The Kadavumbhagam Synagogue, which was recently targeted in an arson attack, is located in Mattancherry, the same locality as the Paradesi Synagogue.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are well-established facts about the Cochin Jewish community and its heritage sites. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Kadavumbhagam Synagogue targeted in the Kochi arson case is situated in Ernakulam's old Jew Street area, a different locality from Mattancherry, where the Paradesi Synagogue stands.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Arson outside synagogue in Kochi: SIT gets five-day custody of accused
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of India's historic minority communities and heritage sites, a theme UPSC has tested through questions on syncretic and diaspora communities

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's monsoon system:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The northeast monsoon, also called the retreating monsoon, is generally more intense than the southwest monsoon over most parts of India.
The northeast monsoon is particularly significant for the rabi crop cycle, while the southwest monsoon is critical for the kharif crop cycle.

El Nino, a phase of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, is associated with warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean and tends to suppress southwest monsoon rainfall over India.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct and standard syllabus facts linking crop cycles to the two monsoon systems and explaining El Nino's suppressive effect on southwest monsoon rainfall, as borne out by this year's 12.6% deficit. Statement 1 is incorrect: the northeast monsoon is less intense than the southwest monsoon, as noted in IMD's own assessment.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Southwest monsoon withdraws from entire country: IMD
questions.pyqLink: Tests the southwest vs northeast monsoon mechanism and ENSO linkage, a perennial physical geography favourite (cf. UPSC questions on El Nino and Indian monsoon)

questions.stem: Consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: India is a founding member of the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI), a multi-stakeholder initiative for the responsible development of artificial intelligence.
Statement-II: The United States, under the current administration, has consistently favoured a binding multilateral treaty to regulate artificial intelligence over voluntary industry self-regulation.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: India has been a founding member of GPAI since its launch in 2020. Statement-II is incorrect: as reflected in the formation of the new federal AI task force, the current US administration has favoured a voluntary industry accord for AI companies to self-police development rather than pushing a binding multilateral treaty.

questions.sourceTitle: Trump names national intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force

questions.stem: With reference to the preparation and revision of electoral rolls in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, an Electoral Registration Officer may delete any name from the electoral roll merely on the basis of an auto-generated field report, without issuing any notice to the elector, provided the deletion is on grounds of shifting of residence.
The Election Commission of India's power of superintendence, direction and control over the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections flows from Article 324 of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is false: the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 require the ERO to issue notice (Form 7/Form 8) and give the elector a reasonable opportunity of being heard before deletion on grounds like shifting of residence, which is precisely the due-process lapse alleged in the Telangana ASDD deletions. Statement 2 is correct: Article 324 vests the ECI with superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: ASDD bulk deletions effected by ECI without due procedure through autogenerated Form-7s signed by EROs
questions.pyqLink: Tests ECI's Article 324 powers and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 — similar to UPSC's recurring questions on ECI's constitutional status and functions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding direct tax collection in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied on the value of taxable securities transactions carried out through a recognised stock exchange.
Securities Transaction Tax is administered by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
Corporate tax is levied on the net income of both domestic and foreign companies operating in India.
Net direct tax collection figures are compiled and released by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) under the Ministry of Finance.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because STT, levied under Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004, is administered by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, not SEBI; SEBI regulates securities markets but has no role in tax administration.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Net direct tax collection grows 13% to ₹13.38 lakh crore till October 14
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of STT's legal basis and administering authority, distinct from corporate/income tax — a recurring near-miss distractor theme in UPSC economy questions.

questions.stem: With reference to India's merchandise trade, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: India's trade deficit for September 2026 narrowed on a year-on-year basis, driven largely by a sharp decline in gold and silver imports.

Merchandise trade data, including export, import and trade deficit figures, are compiled and released by the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics (DGCI&S) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
The trade deficit for September 2026 was narrower than the deficit recorded in August 2026 of the same fiscal year.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the deficit narrowed year-on-year to $30.21 billion from $33 billion, aided by an 81% fall in gold imports. Statement 2 is correct as a static fact about institutional responsibility for trade statistics. Statement 3 is incorrect: the deficit actually widened compared to August 2026 ($26.86 billion), so September's deficit was wider, not narrower, than August's.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's exports jump 23% in September; trade deficit narrows to $30.21 billion
questions.pyqLink: Tests understanding of trade deficit computation and the institutional source of trade data, akin to UPSC's balance-of-payments and external sector questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of historic synagogues in India and the city where each is located:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Paradesi Synagogue (Mattancherry, Kochi, built 1568) and Kadavumbhagam Synagogue (Ernakulam market, Kochi, the over 800-year-old structure in the news) are correctly matched. Beth El Synagogue is actually located in Kolkata, not Mumbai, and Ohel David Synagogue (the 'Lal Deul') is located in Pune, not Ahmedabad — so only two pairs are correct.

questions.sourceTitle: Kochi synagogue arson case: What happened, and history of over 800-year-old structure

questions.stem: Bengaluru experienced heavy rainfall and waterlogging in mid-October. With reference to Indian meteorology, which one of the following best describes the 'post-monsoon' or 'northeast monsoon' rainfall season?
options: It refers to rainfall recorded during the onset phase of the southwest monsoon over the Kerala coast in early June.
It refers to rainfall caused by western disturbances originating in the Mediterranean region that affect north India between December and February.

It refers to rainfall received over southern Peninsular India, mainly Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and parts of Kerala and Karnataka, during October to December as the monsoon trough withdraws southward and draws moisture from the Bay of Bengal.
It refers to convective rainfall confined to the Indo-Gangetic plains triggered by local heating during April and May.
questions.explanation: The correct description is of the northeast/post-monsoon monsoon, which brings October–December rainfall to southern Peninsular India including interior Karnataka as the southwest monsoon withdraws and the wind pattern reverses to draw moisture from the Bay of Bengal. The other options describe the southwest monsoon onset (June), winter western disturbances, and pre-monsoon 'mango shower' convection respectively — all distinct seasonal mechanisms.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Heavy rain snarls traffic, ride-hailing fares surge in Bengaluru
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of India's post-monsoon/northeast monsoon season, a recurring UPSC theme on Indian monsoon mechanisms and regional rainfall distribution.

questions.stem: With reference to the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: It aims to provide vocational training to non-literate, neo-literate, and school dropouts, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.
It is currently administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct and matches the scheme's objective illustrated by the Nilambur tailoring unit for hearing-impaired women. Statement 2 is incorrect: JSS is currently administered by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), having been transferred from the erstwhile Ministry of Human Resource Development.

questions.pyqLink: Tests the nodal ministry and target group of JSS, a recurring theme in UPSC's scheme-based questions testing the sister-scheme/wrong-ministry distractor.

mains.question: Critically examine the procedural safeguards prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 for deletion of names from electoral rolls, and the challenges posed by large-scale automated deletions during a Special Intensive Revision.
